concerns.message: Acceptance 2 says the flare "reaches above the universal anti-air's top edge, so it hits a jumping fighter near the jump apex where the anti-air misses". The height part cannot cause that miss. In duelist.ts the anti-air hitbox covers y 48–144 px. With jumpVelocity 160 and gravity 8, the jump apex is 105 px, and the airborne hurtbox is 80 px tall, so at the apex the jumper covers 105–185 px. That overlaps the anti-air vertically. The anti-air can only miss a jumper because of horizontal reach (x 0–48 px plus an 18 px hurtbox half-width) or because it has only 5 active frames.
concerns.consequence: A worker who makes the flare taller than the anti-air but gives it similar x reach will find the anti-air also hits at the apex. The 'anti-air misses' half of the test then fails, and the worker has to redesign the flare's hitbox or write a test whose stated reason is false. The flare's real advantage has to be longer horizontal reach and/or more active frames, and that must stay within the start-gap reach check (hitbox x+w ≤ 170 px).

concerns.message: The jump-over-bolt punish test needs a much longer Ember cast than §8's floors. A forward jump lasts 40 frames and covers 100 px. The Duelist's heavy has 18 startup frames and reaches 80 px between fighters. A mid bolt must still hit crouchers, so its box starts below 56 px. With a bolt top near 64 px, the jumper is above it only on frames ~8–33 of the jump. Even with an ideally timed scripted jump, the heavy connects about 60 frames (pre-emptive jump) to 70–80 frames (jump when the bolt appears) after the cast starts. That means active + recovery of about 38–58 frames, not the 30-frame floor.
concerns.consequence: A worker who writes near-floor data (22/1/30) fails the jump-over punish test. They then retune the cast length, bolt speed, bolt height and hitstun together while the no-bolt-loop, blockable-at-range and Ember-vs-Duelist tests are already written against the old numbers. That is avoidable rework.

concerns.message: The plan forbids new FighterAction values but says nothing about new DuelEventKind values. `apps/web/src/duelEvents.ts:39-47` looks up a text in an object literal by `event.kind`. That lookup has no fallback: any new kind that is not a key of the object is a typecheck error in a path this lane doesn't own. A bolt clash or a zone cast is an obvious place for a worker to add an event kind.
concerns.consequence: `npm run typecheck` fails in apps/web, which this lane cannot edit, and the run reports `blocked`. Settle it up front: bolt contacts reuse hit, block and guard-break with the bolt's id; bolt-meets-bolt and the zone emit no events.

concerns.message: Recasting while your own bolt or zone is alive is unspecified: refuse the cast, cast with no effect, or replace the old one. So is whether a refused U or I press falls through to other buttons or stays in the buffer. The zone's duration against its cast cycle is not bounded either. If recasting replaces the zone and the zone lasts longer than the cast, Smoke can keep its startups marked as obscured permanently.
concerns.consequence: A permanently smoked Smoke goes against §9's 'no uncounterable invisibility' and §1's 'readable startup'. No test catches it, and fruit-kits-online inherits the mechanic. The choice also changes the matchup and property results, so it should be fixed and written in docs/fruit-kits.md. Suggested: a cast is refused while its slot is filled, and the zone's life is shorter than a named uptime bound.

concerns.message: The bolt contact rules don't cover several cases. (1) A fighter's grab and its own bolt reach the defender on the same frame: is a grab 'melee' for melee priority? (2) A bolt reaches a defender who is thrown, knocked down or in throw-break: the existing detect() ignores strikes on thrown and knocked-down defenders, but the plan doesn't say whether the bolt then dies or passes through. (3) A bolt passes a strike-invulnerable fighter: does it keep going?
concerns.consequence: Each case is decided silently inside the step. The symmetry and property tests pass whatever is chosen, but fruit-kits-online and docs/duel.md then record behaviour that nobody decided. Case (2) matters most: if the bolt passes through, it can hit on the frame knockdown ends, and that edges towards the stun loops §9 forbids.

concerns.message: duelMoveSchema still requires positive `damage` and `hitstun` on every move, `blockstun == active + recovery + advantage` on every non-throw, and a numeric `onBlock`. §8's projectile row uses `projectile-life` and `spacing-dependent`, which duelMoveTimingSchema refuses, so the cast can't reuse the `projectile-special` baseline id. Also, FEINT_REAPPEARANCE_FRAMES is described as 'a named constant', while the constraints say frame data comes from content, not step constants.
concerns.consequence: Without a per-effect refinement, the feint, the bolt cast and the screen cast carry made-up damage, hitstun and blockstun values. That contradicts 'Smoke's specials deal no damage' in the data and misleads the renderer and the docs. If the 12-frame constant lives in step.ts, the schema cannot validate the feint's cancel window against it.

simpler_alternative: Keep the settled design but drop the substep loop. The substep loop is only needed for fast movers. Instead, add schema checks that bound the bolt's speed: (a) bolt speed < bolt width, so two closing bolts overlap at some frame; (b) bolt speed + the fastest fighter speed (dash, walk and pushback) < bolt width + the narrowest hurtbox width. Under those checks, one overlap test per frame at the end-of-move positions gives exactly the swept guarantee, and 'moving apart never falsely meets' holds trivially. Pair it with 'a cast is refused while its own slot is filled', so neither slot is ever replaced, and compute the zone's marks with a function (`inZone(state, index)`) instead of storing them. The whole entity layer is then two nullable slots and one per-frame overlap function, and the symmetry and rollback tests have far fewer edge cases.
cheap_experiment: Before writing any Ember data, spend 15 minutes on the base-commit simulation. Script a Duelist forward jump from 150 px and from 180 px and log y(t), x(t) and the frame the heavy first connects after landing. On the same runs, try the anti-air against a jumper at the apex at x distances of 40–120 px. This gives (1) the shortest cast (startup + active + recovery) that lets the jump-over punish land, likely 60–80 frames rather than 22 + 30; (2) the bolt height and speed range the jumper can clear; and (3) confirmation that the anti-air already covers the apex vertically. With those numbers, the worker would pick a much longer cast recovery and give the flare longer horizontal reach and active frames instead of more height, before the ten-odd scripted tests are written against the wrong data.
